summary: Novelty check + adversarial technical review for the robust-BEV method paper idea

closest_works.name: UniDrive: Towards Universal Driving Perception Across Camera Configurations (Li et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: The closest work to C1. Defines a set of K unified VIRTUAL cameras (intrinsics+extrinsics optimized via CMA-ES to minimize expected projection error) and warps the real rig's images into these virtual views as a plug-and-play pre-processing module at BOTH train and test time. The warp is 'ground-aware projection': per-pixel depth proxy that assumes pixels lie on the ground plane in the near field and on a cylindrical surface at fixed distance D0 in the far field. Evaluated on its own CARLA multi-config benchmark (160k frames, same routes re-driven under different camera configurations); shows a model trained on one configuration generalizes to others with minor degradation.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Same problem statement (cross-camera-configuration generalization for multi-camera BEV perception), same high-level mechanism (input-level virtual-camera canonicalization driven by extrinsics, applied train+test), and same simulator-based evaluation methodology (CARLA re-rendering across rigs). This is the paper we must compare against and differentiate from explicitly; a reviewer will assume C1 == UniDrive unless we say otherwise.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: (1) Geometric exactness: UniDrive re-positions cameras, so its warp needs a depth proxy (ground-plane + cylinder) and produces parallax errors for any off-ground / off-surface content (cars, poles). C1 keeps each physical optical center and changes ONLY rotation (gravity alignment), so the homography is mathematically exact for ALL scene content at ANY depth — no ground-plane assumption, no parallax artifacts. (2) Division of labor: C1 deliberately canonicalizes only what a homography canonicalizes exactly (rotation/gravity); translation and height differences are handled analytically by projection-sampling (C3) and ground-anchored refinement (C5), not by lossy warping. (3) UniDrive presumes CORRECT extrinsics of the deployed rig at test time — it addresses only our CTS-CAL condition and has no answer to VP-IMG (stale extrinsics); our C4 self-calibration converts VP-IMG toward CAL, which UniDrive cannot do by construction. (4) UniDrive's virtual rig is dataset-level and optimized offline; ours is per-view and parameter-free.

closest_works.name: BEV-LaneDet: An Efficient 3D Lane Detection Based on Virtual Camera (Wang et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: The clearest mechanism-level precedent for homography canonicalization. Its 'Virtual Camera' module fixes a standard camera (intrinsics/extrinsics = mean of training-set parameters), selects four points on the road plane, and computes a homography (least squares) from the current camera to the virtual camera; images are warpPerspective'd at both train and inference. Explicitly motivated as 'unifying the in/extrinsic parameters of cameras mounted on different vehicles' to guarantee consistent spatial relationships. Monocular front camera, 3D lane detection, OpenLane/Apollo.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Uses exactly our tool (extrinsics-driven homography warp to a standardized virtual camera, train+test) for exactly our motivation (cross-vehicle camera parameter unification). Any claim that 'homography canonicalization to a virtual camera' per se is new dies here.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: (1) Their homography is a ground-plane (coplanarity) homography that also normalizes camera height/position — exact only for the road plane; fine for lanes painted on the ground, geometrically wrong for 3D objects above it. Our rotation-only gravity-aligned homography is exact for the full scene and we explicitly do NOT warp away height/translation. (2) Single front camera and lane detection only; no multi-camera BEV detection, no surround rig. (3) No test-time calibration question — assumes known correct extrinsics. (4) No cross-rig 3D detection evaluation; we evaluate sedan-to-SUV/bus transfer and re-rendered viewpoint perturbation with measured headroom.

closest_works.name: DG-BEV: Towards Domain Generalization for Multi-view 3D Object Detection in Bird-Eye-View (Wang et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: First DG study for multi-view 3D detection. Three parts: (1) decouples depth estimation from camera intrinsics by predicting scale-invariant depth instead of metric depth (focal-length canonicalization of the regression target); (2) 'dynamic perspective augmentation' — uses homography to synthesize images under perturbed extrinsics (yaw/pitch/roll) at train time; (3) adversarial training over pseudo-domains created by modifying focal length. Cross-dataset evaluation: Waymo, nuScenes, Lyft.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Establishes that homography-warping w.r.t. extrinsics on normal single-rig images is a legitimate, label-preserving way to create viewpoint diversity (our training constraint '2D warps allowed' has precedent), and that intrinsics-decoupled target parameterization helps cross-rig transfer.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: DG-BEV uses homography as random AUGMENTATION (expand the training distribution and hope the network absorbs it), not as CANONICALIZATION (analytically remove the nuisance so the network never sees it); the extrinsic variation is still learned implicitly. No test-time use of geometry, no virtual camera, no treatment of stale extrinsics, and its cross-dataset gaps confound scenery, label policy, and rig — our benchmark isolates the rig variable via re-rendering. Canonicalization vs augmentation is a crisp, testable contrast we can ablate.

closest_works.name: PD-BEV: Towards Generalizable Multi-Camera 3D Object Detection via Perspective Debiasing (Lu et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: Train-time, model-agnostic DG/UDA for multi-camera 3D detection: renders perspective view maps from BEV features through implicit foreground volumes under varied virtual camera poses, and rectifies 'perspective bias' by aligning 3D detections with 2D camera-plane evidence. No inference-time overhead or architecture change. Works for sim-to-real (trained on virtual data only) and cross-dataset settings.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Same goal (viewpoint/camera-parameter-independent features); uses virtual camera poses — but in FEATURE/OUTPUT space (rendering from BEV features) rather than warping input images. We already run this codebase locally as a baseline (Generalizable-BEV).
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: It is a regularizer that encourages invariance statistically; it does not analytically remove extrinsic dependence at the input, does not exploit test-time extrinsics at all, cannot address stale extrinsics (VP-IMG), and was never evaluated on controlled same-scene rig changes. Input-level exact canonicalization + test-time self-calibration remains unclaimed.

closest_works.name: Towards Viewpoint Robustness in Bird's Eye View Segmentation (Klinghoffer et al., NVIDIA)
closest_works.what_it_does: Quantifies that BEV models (Cross View Transformers) trained on one rig collapse under small camera viewpoint changes (e.g., -10 deg pitch => 17% IoU drop), then proposes a novel-view-synthesis method to TRANSFORM the source-rig training data into the TARGET rig's viewpoint and retrains — scaling one labeled dataset to many vehicle types without recollection.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: The motivating phenomenon is identical to our VP/CTS findings (single-rig BEV models are viewpoint-brittle), and it is the standard citation for that claim (in segmentation).
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Their fix requires (a) knowing the target rig at training time and (b) NVS re-rendering of training data per target rig — both excluded by our training constraint (single rig, 2D warps only, no re-rendering, no target-rig knowledge). C1 is target-agnostic canonicalization, not per-target data generation; and they study segmentation, not 3D detection, and never the stale-extrinsics (VP-IMG) case. We also extend the brittleness analysis across 10 detectors with a mechanism-level explanation.

closest_works.name: Metric3D: Towards Zero-shot Metric 3D Prediction from a Single Image (Yin et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: Canonical camera space transformation module (CSTM) for monocular metric depth: transforms every training image (CSTM-image, resize by f_c/f) or its depth labels (CSTM-label, rescale by f_c/f) into a canonical camera with fixed focal length; train and test time. Enables training on 8M+ images across thousands of camera models and zero-shot metric transfer.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Strong precedent that input/label canonicalization to a canonical camera — rather than conditioning on camera parameters — is the winning recipe for cross-camera generalization. We cite it as the intrinsics analogue of what C1 does for rotation.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Canonicalizes INTRINSICS (focal length) only; extrinsics/rotation/gravity are untouched, single-image depth task, no BEV, no multi-camera rig, no detection. Gravity-aligned extrinsic canonicalization for surround-view BEV detection is not covered.

closest_works.name: MoVi-3D: Towards Generalization Across Depth for Monocular 3D Object Detection (Simonelli et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: Generates 'virtual views' at both training and test time in which object appearance is normalized with respect to distance from the camera, relieving the monocular 3D detector from learning depth-specific representations and enabling a lightweight single-stage architecture (KITTI SOTA at the time).
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Earliest 'virtual camera at train AND test time for 3D detection' precedent; canonicalization-not-conditioning philosophy.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Canonicalizes scale/distance within a fixed rig for monocular detection; nothing about extrinsics, gravity, multi-camera rigs, or cross-rig transfer.

closest_works.name: Rotation Matters: Generalized Monocular 3D Object Detection for Various Camera Systems (Lee et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: Analyzes (via depth-map-based re-rendering) which camera pose changes break monocular 3D detection — finds roll/pitch rotation is catastrophic while position/yaw changes are benign — and proposes a TEST-TIME 3D heading/box compensation module that corrects predicted box orientation using the known relative extrinsics between training and deployed cameras; no retraining, no image warping.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Independently establishes our core diagnosis (rotation, i.e., gravity misalignment, is the dominant nuisance across camera systems) and uses known extrinsics analytically at test time.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Output-space compensation only — the backbone still sees rotated images, so the fix is partial; monocular, not surround BEV; no input canonicalization, no self-calibration when extrinsics are stale. C1 removes the nuisance before the network instead of patching predictions after it.

closest_works.name: Gravity/rotation rectification lineage: R2N (Weng et al.), Auto-Rectify Network (Bian et al.), Tilted-image gravity rectifier (Saito et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: R2N estimates in-plane rotation and rectifies CNN features for pedestrian detection under heavy camera rotation (+45%). Auto-Rectify removes relative rotations from handheld indoor video (rotation 'behaves as noise') for self-supervised depth. Saito et al. rectify tilted images to gravity-aligned views (homography from estimated gravity) before monocular depth.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Direct precedent that warping inputs to a gravity-aligned/rotation-canonical frame is an established, repeatedly rediscovered trick across tasks — we should cite this lineage rather than imply we invented gravity rectification.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: All single-camera, non-driving or non-BEV tasks, rotation estimated from image/IMU rather than rig extrinsics, and none address cross-rig 3D detection transfer or interact with a BEV projection geometry. Applying it per-view in a surround rig, sourced from calibrated extrinsics, co-designed with extrinsic-gated BEV sampling, is open.

closest_works.name: BEVHeight (Yang et al.) + MonoUNI (Jia et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: Roadside/infrastructure detection works that canonicalize the REGRESSION TARGET instead of the image: BEVHeight regresses per-pixel height-above-ground instead of depth (distance-agnostic, robust to camera mounting); MonoUNI proposes 'normalized depth' analytically independent of focal length and pitch angle, unifying vehicle-side and infrastructure-side monocular 3D detection.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Precedent for our C3 height-above-ground depth parameterization with analytic metric scale from extrinsics; same philosophy (make learned quantities rig-invariant by construction) applied to outputs.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Target-space canonicalization only — input images remain un-rectified and backbones still absorb viewpoint appearance shift; monocular/roadside settings; no surround multi-camera BEV, no homography input canonicalization, no test-time calibration. These compose with, rather than preempt, C1.

closest_works.name: M-BEV: Masked BEV Perception for Robust Autonomous Driving (Chen et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: Robustness to CAMERA FAILURE (missing views): randomly masks camera-view features during training and reconstructs them from spatio-temporal context (Masked View Reconstruction), e.g., +10.3% mAP for missing back view on PETRv2, nuScenes.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Only the word 'robust' and the multi-camera BEV setting — it perturbs view AVAILABILITY, not view GEOMETRY.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Entirely orthogonal robustness axis; no extrinsic change, no canonicalization, no cross-rig transfer. Cite to delineate the robustness taxonomy (sensor dropout vs sensor configuration shift).

closest_works.name: Negative checks: CBR (calibration-free BEV), PCT, M2BEV / FB-BEV / StreamPETR-PETRv2
closest_works.venue_year: CBR arXiv 2210.17252 (2022); PCT arXiv 2403.12530 (2024); M2BEV arXiv 2022 / FB-BEV ICCV 2023 / PETRv2 ICCV 2023, StreamPETR ICCV 2023
closest_works.what_it_does: CBR drops calibration entirely and learns implicit view mapping (opposite extreme — bakes the training rig into weights, so cross-rig transfer is impossible by construction). PCT improves BEV segmentation under domain shift via perspective-view pseudo-labels but REQUIRES unlabeled target-rig data. M2BEV/FB-BEV contain no canonicalization or virtual-camera component (verified); PETRv2's feature-guided position encoder and StreamPETR's temporal modeling are reported to improve robustness to small extrinsics NOISE only — they condition learned embeddings on extrinsics, which is the rig-conditioned-parameter pattern our C2/C3 argue against (zero variance under single-rig training).
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: These are the families a reviewer might name-drop; none performs extrinsics-driven input canonicalization and none evaluates same-scene rig swaps.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Confirms the gap: between 'condition on calibration' (PETR-style, saturates on single-rig data — our BN(27) finding), 'ignore calibration' (CBR), 'augment' (DG-BEV), 'regularize' (PD-BEV, PCT), and 'depth-proxy virtual rig' (UniDrive), the exact rotation-only gravity-aligned canonicalization + analytic translation handling + test-time self-calibration slot is unoccupied.

litCanon.verdict: C1 as a bare idea — "warp images to a standardized virtual camera using extrinsics, at train and test time" — is NOT novel: BEV-LaneDet (CVPR 2023) does precisely this with a ground-plane homography for monocular 3D lanes, and UniDrive (ICLR 2025) does it for full surround-view 3D perception on a CARLA cross-configuration benchmark that closely mirrors ours, so C1 cannot carry a paper alone and UniDrive must be cited, compared against (ideally run as a baseline — it is plug-and-play), and differentiated in the first paragraph of related work. What survives is a sharp, defensible design distinction: both precedents warp to virtual cameras at DIFFERENT positions, which forces a scene-geometry assumption (BEV-LaneDet: road-plane coplanarity; UniDrive: ground-plane + cylinder depth proxy) that is exact only for ground content and introduces parallax error on the 3D objects we actually detect; C1 instead restricts canonicalization to the rotation-only (gravity-alignment) component, for which the homography is mathematically exact at all depths, and deliberately routes the non-canonicalizable residual (camera height/translation) through analytic projection (C3) and refinement (C5) rather than lossy warping — "canonicalize exactly what is exactly canonicalizable, handle the rest analytically" is a crisp principle no prior work states or ablates. Additionally, every input-canonicalization precedent (UniDrive, BEV-LaneDet, Metric3D) presumes CORRECT test-time camera parameters, i.e., they only address our CTS-CAL condition; none can touch VP-IMG (stale extrinsics), which is where C1 becomes load-bearing as the substrate that makes C4's test-time rotation self-calibration analytic (pure-rotation candidates = exact homographies on cached features). Verdict: C1 is incremental in isolation (a known mechanism with a better-justified geometric instantiation) and should be positioned as a co-carrying component — the paper's novelty must be carried by the system claim (single-rig-trained, target-rig-agnostic transfer combining exact rotation canonicalization C1 + variance-aware conditioning C2/C3 + test-time self-calibration C4/C5) plus the cross-model mechanism analysis, with explicit ablations of canonicalization-vs-augmentation (vs DG-BEV) and rotation-only-vs-repositioned virtual cameras (vs UniDrive) to evidence the distinction. Sources: arxiv.org/abs/2410.13864 (UniDrive), arxiv.org/abs/2210.06006 (BEV-LaneDet), arxiv.org/abs/2303.01686 (DG-BEV), arxiv.org/abs/2310.11346 (PD-BEV), arxiv.org/abs/2309.05192 (NVIDIA viewpoint robustness), arxiv.org/abs/2307.10984 (Metric3D), arxiv.org/abs/1912.08035 (MoVi-3D), arxiv.org/abs/2310.05366 (Rotation Matters), arxiv.org/abs/1706.08917 (R2N), arxiv.org/abs/2006.02708 (Auto-Rectify), arxiv.org/abs/2303.08498 (BEVHeight), MonoUNI NeurIPS 2023 proceedings, arxiv.org/abs/2312.12144 (M-BEV), arxiv.org/abs/2210.17252 (CBR), arxiv.org/abs/2403.12530 (PCT).

closest_works.name: LCCNet (lineage: RegNet 2017, CalibNet IROS 2018, CalibRefine arXiv:2502.17648)
closest_works.venue_year: CVPR 2021 Workshops (WAD); CalibNet IROS 2018; CalibRefine arXiv 2025
closest_works.what_it_does: LiDAR-camera extrinsic self-calibration: regresses the DECALIBRATION DEVIATION (delta-R, delta-t, 6-DoF) from an initial extrinsic guess, trained by synthetically de-calibrating ground-truth extrinsics; uses cost-volume feature matching between RGB and projected depth, with ITERATIVE refinement at inference (coarse-to-fine cascade of networks for shrinking error ranges).
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Closest mechanical precedent for our fine stage: delta-correction relative to assumed extrinsics, supervision from synthetic perturbations, iterative test-time refinement. The coarse-to-fine cascade parallels our sweep-then-regress structure.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Requires LiDAR as the metric anchor — our setting is camera-only with no second modality; nothing anchors the correction except image content + cross-view/ground constraints. Ours is embedded in a BEV detector (re-runs only the BEV encoder on cached backbone features) and is scored by a detection-task-coupled learned BEV scorer, not photometric/cost-volume matching. Estimation target is rotation-only delta per rig, matching the VP-IMG failure mode we measured.

closest_works.name: BEVCalib: LiDAR-Camera Calibration via Geometry-Guided Bird's-Eye View Representations (Yuan et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: First calibration network operating in BEV space: fuses camera-BEV and LiDAR-BEV features and decodes extrinsics with a geometry-guided BEV decoder + feature selector; trained with synthetic noise on KITTI/nuScenes; large gains over LCCNet-style baselines.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Uses BEV-space representations to decode calibration — superficially close to our 'learned BEV scorer over Delta-R candidates'. Confirms BEV features carry a strong calibration signal.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Still LiDAR-camera (cross-modal registration gives the supervision signal); it REGRESSES calibration as a standalone task, never couples to downstream detection quality. We have no LiDAR; our scorer is a discriminative evaluator over analytically-applied rotation hypotheses with the perception model in the loop, and we report the downstream detection recovery (VP-IMG -> CAL, RRS 0.425 -> 0.779), which no calibration paper measures.

closest_works.name: GeoCalib (Veicht et al.) and Perspective Fields (Jin et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: Single-image estimation of camera-to-gravity rotation (roll/pitch) + FoV. Trained on crops of gravity-aligned 360-degree panoramas with roll/pitch/FoV sampled uniformly — i.e., supervision IS synthetic rotational warps. GeoCalib adds a differentiable Levenberg-Marquardt optimizer over a predicted perspective field.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Direct precedent for our fine Delta-R regressor's supervision recipe (pure-rotation = exact homography, so labels are free from single-rig images) and for rotation-only as the tractable target. GeoCalib's optimize-over-candidates-with-learned-confidence is philosophically close to our sweep+scorer.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: These are standalone, single-image, absolute (gravity-relative) estimators with no notion of a multi-camera rig, no cross-view consistency, no delta relative to assumed rig extrinsics, and no downstream 3D-detection coupling. Yaw (heading) is unobservable for them; our rig-level cross-view consistency and BEV scoring recover it. Integration with cached detector features for cheap candidate evaluation is new.

closest_works.name: CLGo: Learning to Predict 3D Lane Shape and Camera Pose from a Single Image via Geometry Constraints (Liu et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: Two-stage pose-then-perceive for monocular 3D lane detection: stage 1 predicts camera pitch/height from the image (with geometry-constraint multi-task training and pose augmentation); stage 2 warps to a top view with the ESTIMATED pose and detects 3D lanes. Beats perfect-pose baselines without GT pose.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: The clearest precedent for 'estimate extrinsics at test time, then run BEV-style perception with the corrected geometry' — same conversion of stale/unknown pose into usable pose for a downstream driving task.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Monocular, lane-only, ground-plane-constrained, pitch+height only; feed-forward regression with no candidate sweep, no learned BEV scorer, no iterative refinement, no cross-view consistency (single camera), and never evaluated for multi-camera 3D object detection or on re-rendered viewpoint shifts. We generalize this idea to full surround-view 3D detection with a measured headroom target.

closest_works.name: OECS / ROECS: Online Extrinsics Correction for the Surround-view System (Zhang et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: Classical (non-deep) online correction of surround-view fisheye extrinsics after bumps/collisions: minimizes photometric 'bi-camera error' between ground-plane projections of adjacent overlapping cameras (semi-direct sparse optimization).
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Same problem statement as C4 (extrinsics drifted in the field, correct them online from images alone, multi-camera rig) and same key signal as our gating term: cross-view consistency on the ground.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Photometric, requires overlapping FoV with textured ground, optimizes a hand-crafted energy, targets the stitched AVM image — never a learned BEV perception model. Our learned BEV scorer works where photometric overlap is thin (typical 6-cam rigs), and our objective is detection performance, not stitching quality.

closest_works.name: SensorX2car (OpenCalib/PJLab) and Self-Supervised Online Camera Calibration (Hogan, Sistu, Eising)
closest_works.what_it_does: Online camera-to-vehicle rotation calibration in road scenes: deep nets detect the dominant vanishing point + horizon line (1 VP gives only 2 rotational DoF; horizon supplies the third) to recover yaw/pitch/roll while driving; the Valeo work learns intrinsics+extrinsics self-supervised in real time for driving/parking systems.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Covers the exact 'rotation from VP/horizon, online, no targets' design space the user asked about; confirms rotation-only is the established online-recoverable component (translation/height needs odometry or ground priors).
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Standalone calibration utilities relying on hand-picked geometric cues (VP/horizon exist only in favorable scenes); per-camera, no rig-level consistency; output never validated by, or coupled to, a 3D detector. Our scorer evaluates hypotheses by what the detector actually needs, and works per-rig rather than per-scene-cue.

closest_works.name: Calibration-free / extrinsic-decoupled BEV detectors: CFT (arXiv:2210.17252), Decoupled Ray Transformation (Image and Vision Computing 2025, S0262885625000162)
closest_works.venue_year: arXiv 2022; Image and Vision Computing, Jan 2025
closest_works.what_it_does: Remove dependence on extrinsics instead of correcting them: CFT learns an implicit view-to-BEV mapping with no camera parameters; the IVC 2025 paper decouples ray transformation from extrinsics so detection degrades less under calibration noise. Both report robustness to extrinsic perturbation (CFT: BEVFormer drops 0.6-6.8% NDS, PETR 4.7-7.6%, CFT ~stable).
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Same evaluation axis (noisy/stale extrinsics at test time) and the main competing philosophy to C4: invariance-by-architecture vs. our estimate-and-correct.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Implicit mappings memorize the training rig (they cannot transfer to a NEW platform with CORRECT extrinsics — our CTS-CAL setting — because there is no input through which correct extrinsics can help). C4 keeps analytic geometry so corrected extrinsics are immediately usable; nobody in this line outputs corrected extrinsics or exploits a known headroom between stale and correct calibration.

closest_works.name: Extrinsic-noise-robust detection with KNOWN deviation: GARKT (tire blow-out); plus PETRv2 / CAPE noise analyses
closest_works.what_it_does: GARKT models camera deviation from tire blow-out (per-camera Gaussian rot/trans noise) and enlarges deformable receptive fields (auto-resizable kernels) per severity level — severity comes from tire-pressure sensors, so the deviation is externally signaled, not estimated. PETRv2/CAPE inject extrinsic noise during training and encode extrinsics in feature/positional space to be less sensitive.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: These are the 'ADD a module to tolerate noisy extrinsics' papers the user asked about; they define the perturbation protocol (synthetic rot/trans noise on nuScenes) most reviewers will know.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: All of them either assume the deviation is known/sensed (GARKT) or merely soften sensitivity via training-time noise augmentation (PETRv2/CAPE); none ESTIMATE the correction at test time, and all evaluate on copy-paste noise of extrinsic matrices with UNCHANGED images — our re-rendered VP-IMG (images actually shifted, extrinsics stale) is the physically consistent version of this test, which no prior work constructs or corrects.

closest_works.name: MonoTTA: Fully Test-Time Adaptation for Monocular 3D Object Detection (Lin et al.)
closest_works.what_it_does: Adapts a mono 3D detector to OOD test data without labels by reliability-driven self-training on high-score objects + negative learning on low-score ones; updates network WEIGHTS online (KITTI/nuScenes corruption shifts).
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Establishes test-time adaptation for camera 3D detection as a recognized paradigm; our C4 is the geometric counterpart in this space.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Adapts parameters, not geometry — it cannot fix a wrong projection matrix and was never tested on calibration/viewpoint shift. C4 keeps weights frozen and searches/regresses an interpretable, low-dimensional geometric variable (Delta-R), which is the right inductive bias when the shift IS geometric; this distinction is clean and defensible.

closest_works.name: RoboBEV benchmark (Xie et al., TPAMI 2025) and RoboDrive Challenge (ICRA 2024, arXiv:2405.08816)
closest_works.what_it_does: Largest robustness benchmarks for camera BEV perception: 8 natural corruptions + camera crash/frame-lost over 33 models; RoboDrive ran 5 robust-perception tracks with 18 camera corruption/failure cases. Winning entries (e.g., TSMA-BEV: FFT-based augmentation + sequential consistency) rely on augmentation/ensembling.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: The robustness-benchmark line our paper will be compared to; we checked specifically — neither the corruption taxonomy nor any reported challenge solution includes extrinsic decalibration as a corruption or test-time calibration correction as a remedy.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Their corruptions are photometric/temporal/sensor-dropout; geometric miscalibration with physically consistent re-rendered images is absent. This confirms both our benchmark axis (VP-IMG vs CTS-CAL) and our remedy (C4) are unoccupied in the strongest existing robustness line — a citable gap.

closest_works.name: Viewpoint-robustness-by-training line: Klinghoffer et al. (NVIDIA), VEDet, UniDrive
closest_works.what_it_does: Klinghoffer: shows BEV segmentation collapses under small test-time pitch/yaw/height changes and fixes it with NeRF-style novel-view-synthesis augmentation to the target rig. VEDet: trains viewpoint equivariance with virtual frames + view-conditioned queries. UniDrive: projects all images to unified virtual cameras (ground-aware) and optimizes virtual configs — but assumes test-time extrinsics are KNOWN and correct.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Same failure phenomenon and (UniDrive) virtual-camera machinery overlapping our C1; Klinghoffer's CARLA/DRIVE-Sim re-rendered viewpoint data is the closest existing benchmark to our VP protocol.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: All three operate at TRAINING time and/or require correct extrinsics at test time; none addresses the stale-extrinsics case (images moved, model not told). C4 is complementary and orthogonal: it recovers the correct extrinsics that these methods presuppose. Our framing — measuring the IMG-to-CAL headroom per model and then closing it — does not exist in any of them.

litSelfcal.verdict: C4 is novel as a system-in-context but not as a primitive, and it is strong enough to CO-CARRY the paper next to the benchmark — not to carry one alone. Every ingredient has a precedent we must cite and differentiate: delta-extrinsic regression trained on synthetic decalibration with iterative refinement (LCCNet, CVPRW 2021; CalibNet, IROS 2018), calibration decoding from BEV features (BEVCalib, CoRL 2025), rotation-only estimation supervised by synthetic rotational warps of single-rig images (Perspective Fields, CVPR 2023; GeoCalib, ECCV 2024), pose-then-perceive for a downstream driving task (CLGo, AAAI 2022), and online surround-view extrinsic correction via cross-view ground consistency (OECS/ROECS, ICIP 2020/ACM MM 2021). What no prior work does — verified across the calibration, robust-BEV, TTA, and robustness-benchmark literatures — is (a) camera-only test-time extrinsic correction COUPLED INTO a multi-camera BEV 3D detector, (b) a hypothesis-sweep stage where rotation candidates are applied analytically and scored by a learned BEV scorer while re-running only the BEV encoder on cached backbone features (the existing robust-BEV papers either assume the deviation is externally known, e.g. GARKT, or train for invariance, e.g. PETRv2/CAPE/CFT, and never output corrected extrinsics; MonoTTA adapts weights, not geometry; RoboBEV/RoboDrive contain no decalibration corruption at all), and (c) the benchmark-measured headroom framing: physically consistent re-rendered VP-IMG vs CTS-CAL, quantifying exactly how much a calibration fix can recover (RRS 0.425 -> 0.779) and then closing that gap. That framing is C4's strongest, most defensible claim — it converts 'we built a calibrator' into 'we identified and closed a measured failure mode', which nobody in the LCCNet/BEVCalib line can claim because they never measure downstream detection. Risks to manage: a reviewer will say 'LCCNet + GeoCalib glued onto BEVFormer', so the ablation must show the BEV-scorer sweep beats (i) feed-forward regression alone (GeoCalib-style) and (ii) photometric/feature-matching scoring (ROECS-style); also the claimed GaussianLSS PitchBinClassifier precedent does not appear in the GaussianLSS paper (CVPR 2025, arXiv:2504.01957) — it may exist only in the repo code, so verify before citing it as the scorer precedent; and the inaccessible IVC 2025 'decoupled ray transformation' paper should be obtained and checked, since its abstract is the nearest invariance-based competitor claim.

closest_works.name: BEVHeight (Yang et al., arXiv 2303.08498)
closest_works.what_it_does: Roadside (pole-mounted, 'a few meters above the ground', looking down) detector that regresses per-pixel categorical HEIGHT-to-ground distribution instead of depth, then lifts via wedge-shaped voxels using similar-triangle projection in a gravity-aligned virtual coordinate system (Y-axis perpendicular to ground). Motivation: per-pixel depth difference d−d' 'would drastically decrease when the car moves away from the camera' while 'the height to the ground is consistent regardless of the distance'.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Direct precedent for BOTH halves of our pitch: (a) height-above-ground parameterization with analytic (extrinsics-driven) mapping to 3D, and (b) an explicit ROBUSTNESS-TO-EXTRINSICS claim — under N(0,1.67°) roll/pitch noise BEVDepth collapses 60.75%→9.48% AP(veh) while BEVHeight keeps 51.77% (+42.3%). This is essentially our VP-CAL/EXT robustness argument, already published. It also already uses a gravity-aligned virtual frame (overlaps C1 in spirit).
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: CRITICAL: BEVHeight is explicitly contraindicated in OUR regime. Verbatim from the paper: 'our methods fall behind the traditional BEVDepth on the ego-vehicle settings by 2%... is not ideal on cameras mounted on ego-vehicles', and 'the distance between the predicted point and ground-truth is inversely proportional to the camera ground height'. For a vehicle cam at H≈1.6m the inverse mapping r=(H−h)/sinθ has ∂r/∂h = −r/(H−h): a car roofline at h≈1.4m, r=40m amplifies height error ×200, and exactly at the horizon (h→H) height carries ZERO range information. So 'height for vehicle-mounted cameras' is not occupied territory — but only because the published evidence says it loses accuracy there. We must (i) show the weight-path/gating use (not BEVHeight's forward splatting) degrades gracefully to plain projection-sampling near the horizon instead of producing wrong geometry, and (ii) win the rig-transfer trade (height is rig-invariant; depth is not) with cross-rig numbers BEVHeight never reports (it only tests rotational NOISE on the same roadside rig, never new camera HEIGHT/platform, never single-rig→new-rig).

closest_works.name: BEVHeight++ (Yang et al., arXiv 2309.16179)
closest_works.what_it_does: Extends BEVHeight to ego-vehicle (nuScenes) by FUSING a height branch and a depth branch: image-level concat of height distribution with context features plus BEV-level deformable cross-attention between height-based and depth-based BEV features (+1.9 NDS over BEVDepth on nuScenes val). States verbatim: 'the height-based pipeline is more suitable for higher-position roadside cameras and is not friendly to the lowest-positioned ego-vehicle cameras' and 'for the same height prediction error |h_gt − h_pred|, the distance between the predicted point and ground-truth is inversely proportional to the camera ground height'. Robustness: ~57% improvement over baselines under 1.67° roll/pitch perturbation.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: The authors' own answer to the vehicle-mounted regime: they did NOT keep pure height — they added depth back. Also overlaps our extrinsics-robustness story (Fig. 3: height distributions overlap strongly between clean and perturbed extrinsics; depth distributions do not). No camera-parameter conditioning of any network — robustness comes purely from the parameterization, which is our C3 thesis too.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: BEVHeight++ fuses in FEATURE space (splat/concat); it does not gate attention weights, does not condition on ray direction, does not canonicalize inputs, and never evaluates cross-rig transfer (new camera height/platform) — only same-rig rotational noise. Our single-rig-training → new-rig-evaluation protocol and the 'learn only rig-invariant quantities (per-pixel ray + height), map to metric 3D analytically per current extrinsics' principle remain unclaimed. But we should mirror their hybrid: pure height gating near the horizon is uninformative, so a height-where-well-conditioned / depth-or-disparity-near-horizon gating (or their dual-branch) is the defensible design.

closest_works.name: DFA3D (Li et al., arXiv 2307.12972; code IDEA-Research/3D-deformable-attention)
closest_works.what_it_does: 3D deformable attention for 2D→3D lifting, implemented as mathematically equivalent DEPTH-WEIGHTED 2D deformable attention: a per-pixel depth distribution multiplies the deformable attention weights (verified in our local fork: weight_update = depth_score.mean(dim=-1) * attention_weights, BEVFormer_DFA3D/.../spatial_cross_attention.py:579). +1.41 mAP avg on BEVFormer-style models, up to +15.1 with GT depth.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: This IS our C3 mechanism — 'depth predicted as distribution used only to gate deformable-attention weights' is exactly DFA3D's weight path, and we even build on its codebase (already trained on CARLA per our own logs). The gating mechanism itself contributes zero novelty.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: DFA3D gates with METRIC DEPTH (LiDAR-supervised depth net, rig-specific, no camera conditioning analysis); we re-parameterize the gated distribution as height-above-ground with scale supplied analytically by extrinsics, condition the predictor only on per-pixel ray direction, and motivate both via single-rig variance analysis. Novelty must be framed as 'what to gate with for cross-rig robustness', not 'gating'. Bonus: our own cross-model finding (gates-sampling vs extract-then-place) gives a measured reason why the weight-path is the right place to inject geometry.

closest_works.name: HeightFormer (Wu et al., arXiv 2307.13510)
closest_works.what_it_does: VEHICLE-mounted (nuScenes) camera-only detector that models HEIGHT explicitly in BEV space (self-recursive height + uncertainty estimation guiding reference points), arguing height needs no LiDAR supervision and — notably — that 'no matter which kind of camera configuration is used, the height condition is processed with the same pattern', i.e., height 'can fit arbitrary camera rigs'. Includes a proof of equivalence between height-based and depth-based formulations. 59.8 NDS test.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Closest claim-level overlap for 'height generalizes across camera rigs' on vehicle-mounted platforms. If a reviewer knows one paper against our C3 framing, it is this one.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: It models height per-BEV-cell from BEV annotations (label-space argument: height labels are rig-independent), not a per-PIXEL height distribution gating image-feature attention; it has no ray-direction conditioning, no analytic extrinsic scale path, and crucially it never TESTS cross-rig transfer — the 'arbitrary rigs' claim is asserted, not measured. Our re-rendered VP-IMG / CTS-CAL benchmark turns their assertion into the experiment they didn't run; we should cite their equivalence proof and rebut it for the perturbed-extrinsics case (equivalence holds only when train/test extrinsics match).

closest_works.name: CoBEV (Shi et al., arXiv 2310.02815)
closest_works.what_it_does: Roadside detector estimating BOTH per-pixel depth and height distributions, lifting with each and fusing via two-stage complementary feature selection; characterizes depth as geometry-centric and height as semantic-centric/category-discriminative; shows SOTA across camera-distance ranges, heterologous (cross-dataset/cross-scene) settings and noisy camera parameters.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Established that height and depth distributions are complementary and that height helps under noisy camera parameters — pre-empts a pure 'height beats depth' ablation story.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Roadside-only, LSS-style forward splatting (not attention gating), no ray conditioning, no single-rig training constraint, no vehicle-platform transfer. Also a useful citation FOR us: its depth=geometry/height=semantics analysis supports a hybrid gating design near the horizon.

closest_works.name: Metric3D / Metric3Dv2 (Yin et al., arXiv 2307.10984; 2404.15506)
closest_works.what_it_does: Zero-shot metric monocular depth via Canonical Camera Space Transformation (CSTM): rescale either the image (CSTM-image) or the depth labels (CSTM-label) by the ratio of canonical to actual focal length, so all data appears captured by one canonical camera; de-canonicalize predictions analytically at test time. Enables training on 8M images/11 datasets and transfer to unseen cameras.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: The cleanest published precedent for 'canonicalize analytically, learn only the canonical problem, invert analytically at test time' — the design principle behind our C1+C3 scale path. We should cite it as the principle's origin.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: CSTM canonicalizes INTRINSICS ONLY (focal-length metric ambiguity); camera height and rotation are extrinsics and are untouched — so Metric3D is the right PRINCIPLE precedent but NOT a prior solution to camera-height change. Our extension of the canonicalization idea to the extrinsic rig (gravity-aligned homography for rotation in C1, height-above-ground with extrinsics-supplied scale in C3) inside a multi-view BEV detector is not done there. Answer to the posed question: yes, Metric3D-style canonicalization is the stronger ANALYTIC-handling precedent than BEVHeight for camera-height changes, but it must be cited as principle, with GVDepth/FUMET as the height-specific instances.

closest_works.name: UniDepth (Piccinelli et al., arXiv 2403.18913)
closest_works.what_it_does: Universal monocular metric depth: a self-promptable camera module predicts a dense per-pixel ray representation (azimuth/elevation angles), depth is predicted in a pseudo-spherical (ray-conditioned) output space, and a geometric invariance loss enforces camera-prompt-invariant depth features.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Direct precedent for 'condition learned modules on per-pixel ray direction' — ray-angle conditioning of depth features is its core mechanism. Together with CAM-Convs (Facil et al., CVPR 2019: per-pixel coordinate/FOV maps fed into convolutions to generalize depth across intrinsics) and DD3D-style focal scaling, ray conditioning per se is well-trodden in monocular depth.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: These works condition on rays to generalize across INTRINSICS/FOV in monocular depth foundation models. None operate inside a multi-camera BEV detector, none make our negative argument — that rig-LEVEL conditioning vectors (camera height, global rotation) are degenerate under single-rig training (our code-verified BEVDepth BN(27)+MLP saturation at 19–784σ on novel calib) — and none restrict conditioning to within-rig-variant inputs as a stated design rule. The 'zero-variance features under single-rig training' analysis is our sharpest novel claim here.

closest_works.name: GVDepth (arXiv 2412.06080)
closest_works.what_it_does: Zero-shot metric monocular depth for GROUND VEHICLES: a canonical representation embedding camera-to-ground-plane geometry ('depth regression via vertical image positions of objects', i.e., ground-anchored), probabilistically fused with an object-size cue; trained on a SINGLE dataset with a SINGLE camera setup, evaluated zero-shot on five AD datasets with different rigs; notes the vertical-position cue 'is highly susceptible to overfitting', motivating the canonicalization.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: The strongest precedent for our exact protocol — single-camera-setup training, transfer to unseen rigs (including height changes) — and for ground-plane-anchored canonical depth. Its two-cue probabilistic fusion is essentially the depth-vs-height conditioning trade we face, solved by fusing. Also relevant to C5's ground anchoring. Related: FUMET ('Camera Height Doesn't Change', Kinoshita & Nishino, ECCV 2024) uses fixed camera height as the metric scale anchor for unsupervised road-scene depth.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Monocular DEPTH estimation, not multi-camera BEV 3D detection: no BEV encoder, no attention gating, no multi-view extrinsics consumption, no detection metrics. Porting the canonical ground-anchored parameterization into the deformable-attention gating path of a surround-view detector, under re-rendered viewpoint perturbation evaluation, remains ours — but we must cite GVDepth or risk a 'already done for depth' review.

closest_works.name: MonoUNI (Jia et al., NeurIPS 2023) + DG-BEV (Wang et al., arXiv 2303.01686, CVPR 2023)
closest_works.what_it_does: MonoUNI: unifies vehicle-side and infrastructure-side monocular 3D detection with 'normalized depth' — an optimization target made independent of focal length AND pitch angle, explicitly so that depth learning is not disturbed by camera-geometry diversity across the two sides. DG-BEV: domain generalization for multi-view BEV detection by decoupling depth from focal length (scale-invariant/virtual depth) plus dynamic perspective augmentation of extrinsics and adversarial pseudo-domains; the same virtual-depth idea recurs in PD-BEV/Perspective Debiasing (arXiv 2310.11346, in our repo as Generalizable-BEV).
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: MonoUNI proves the community already re-parameterized the depth TARGET to absorb pitch and focal analytically — close in spirit to 'height target absorbs rig geometry'. DG-BEV/PD-BEV are the existing BEV-detector answers to cross-rig depth generalization and will be the baselines reviewers name.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: MonoUNI normalizes for pitch/focal but NOT camera height, is monocular, and spans exactly two known regimes rather than continuous rig perturbation. DG-BEV/PD-BEV decouple INTRINSICS and rely on augmentation/adversarial training for extrinsics — they keep metric-depth lifting and do not touch the attention-gating path, height parameterization, or ray-only conditioning; neither trains under our single-rig/no-multi-rig-data constraint with re-rendered VP evaluation. We should benchmark against PD-BEV (already set up in pdbev-b200) to show C3 beats augmentation-based DG.

litHeight.verdict: C3 is a composition of individually well-precedented ingredients — the gating mechanism is literally DFA3D (ICCV'23, we run its code), height-above-ground distributions are BEVHeight/BEVHeight++/CoBEV/HeightFormer, ray-direction conditioning is CAM-Convs/UniDepth, and analytic canonicalize-then-invert is Metric3D's CSTM — so no single ingredient can carry a paper, and reviewers will assemble this list quickly. What IS novel and defensible: (1) the specific composition inside a multi-camera BEV detector under a single-rig training constraint with measured cross-rig transfer (no prior work evaluates height-parameterized lifting on re-rendered viewpoint perturbations or platform transfer; BEVHeight only tested 1.67° rotational noise on the same roadside rig, HeightFormer asserts 'fits arbitrary rigs' without ever testing it); and (2) the variance-based conditioning rule — never condition on rig-level vectors because single-rig training gives them zero variance — backed by our code-verified BN(27) saturation evidence, which no prior work states or measures. However, there is a serious technical landmine the proposal must defuse head-on: BEVHeight's own published text says the height formulation 'is not ideal on cameras mounted on ego-vehicles' (−2% vs BEVDepth on nuScenes) because localization error from a fixed height error 'is inversely proportional to the camera ground height' — for a 1.6m-high vehicle camera, r=(H−h)/sinθ gives ∂r/∂h≈−r/(H−h) (≈×200 amplification for a 1.4m roofline at 40m), and height is exactly singular (zero range information) on horizon rays, which is where distant objects live in our regime; BEVHeight++ 'fixed' this by re-adding a depth branch. Our weight-path use partially escapes this — gating with an uninformative height distribution degrades to plain BEVFormer projection-sampling rather than misplacing geometry, and the rig-INVARIANCE of the height target (the thing that matters for VP-IMG/CTS-CAL) survives — but in-distribution accuracy will likely pay near the horizon, so plan either an elevation-dependent hybrid (height gating off-horizon, depth/disparity gating near-horizon, per CoBEV/BEVHeight++ complementarity) or an explicit accuracy-vs-robustness trade ablation. Verdict: C3 is incremental as a standalone contribution but can CO-CARRY the paper if reframed from 'height instead of depth' (occupied, and contraindicated in our regime by BEVHeight's own results) to 'rig-invariant parameterization + ray-only conditioning of the gating path, with metric scale restored analytically from extrinsics' — i.e., Metric3D-style canonicalization extended from intrinsics to the extrinsic rig — validated by the cross-rig experiments every prior height paper skipped, and with GVDepth/FUMET cited as the camera-height canonicalization precedents from monocular depth. Sources: arxiv.org/abs/2303.08498 (BEVHeight, quotes via ar5iv), arxiv.org/abs/2309.16179 (BEVHeight++, quotes via ar5iv), arxiv.org/abs/2307.12972 (DFA3D), arxiv.org/abs/2307.13510 (HeightFormer), arxiv.org/abs/2310.02815 (CoBEV), arxiv.org/abs/2307.10984 + 2404.15506 (Metric3D/v2), arxiv.org/abs/2403.18913 (UniDepth), arxiv.org/abs/1904.02028 (CAM-Convs), arxiv.org/abs/2412.06080 (GVDepth), arxiv.org/abs/2312.04530 (FUMET ECCV'24), NeurIPS 2023 MonoUNI (proceedings.neurips.cc), arxiv.org/abs/2303.01686 (DG-BEV), arxiv.org/abs/2310.11346 (PD-BEV); local code verification: /home/hanyan_arch/viewpoint/BEVFormer/3D-deformable-attention/BEVFormer_DFA3D/projects/mmdet3d_plugin/bevformer/modules/spatial_cross_attention.py:579.

closest_works.name: Towards Viewpoint Robustness in Bird's Eye View Segmentation (Klinghoffer et al., NVIDIA; arXiv 2309.05192)
closest_works.what_it_does: First paper to isolate the structured-viewpoint-shift threat model: small pitch/yaw/height/depth changes to the camera rig cause large BEV segmentation drops EVEN when the model is given the updated extrinsics (their CARLA release stores adjusted extrinsics per viewpoint, i.e. their setting is our VP-CAL/CTS-CAL, not VP-IMG). Fix is training-time: a novel-view-synthesis method (Worldsheet-based) transforms source-rig data to a known target rig, recovering ~14.7% of lost IoU on average. CARLA + DriveSim, segmentation only.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Defines essentially our problem (single-rig training, cross-rig deployment) and our diagnosis (models overfit the training rig). Their 36-viewpoint CARLA protocol is the direct ancestor of our VP benchmark.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Their fix is NVS re-rendering for augmentation — exactly what our training constraint forbids — and it requires knowing the target rig a priori and retraining per rig. They never test stale extrinsics (VP-IMG), propose no architectural invariance and no test-time component, and only do segmentation. We must cite it as the philosophical origin and beat the 'just synthesize the target rig' alternative in the rig-unknown setting. Note its follow-up PCT (arXiv 2403.12530) drifted to SSL/UDA, so the line is not actively occupied.

closest_works.name: CoIn3D: Revisiting Configuration-Invariant Multi-Camera 3D Object Detection (arXiv 2603.05042)
closest_works.what_it_does: Cross-configuration 3D detection across nuScenes/Waymo/Lyft under three paradigms (BEVDepth, BEVFormer, PETR). Two components: (1) SFM — injects per-pixel inverse-focal map, ground-plane depth map, ground gradient map, and Plücker raymap into image features; (2) CDA — training-free 3DGS-style point rendering of SOURCE-rig annotated frames (TSDF + depth completion) to synthesize full RGB images under random novel intrinsics/extrinsics/layouts at ~450 fps. Big gains: BEVDepth nuScenes→Waymo mAP 0.040→0.381, NDS* 0.178→0.513, beating DG-BEV/PD-BEV/UDGA and input-warping baselines incl. UniDrive.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Heaviest overlap and most dangerous competitor. Their Plücker-ray + ground-depth conditioning is our C3 'condition only on per-pixel ray direction' and our C5 ground anchoring; their CDA is viewpoint augmentation from single-rig data; they test correct target calibration = our CTS-CAL. They also span the same three paradigms we benchmark.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: They never evaluate stale extrinsics (VP-IMG) and have no test-time calibration (C4/C5) — inference simply trusts ground-truth target calib. Their CDA IS re-rendering (needs depth completion/meshing), so under our no-rendering constraint our recipe is differentiated, BUT CDA needs no multi-rig collection either, which weakens 'no re-rendering' as a practical motivation — we must either beat CDA empirically on our benchmark or argue renderer-artifact/deployment grounds. Their cross-dataset protocol conflates content and rig gaps; our CARLA same-content re-render isolates the rig channel cleanly.

closest_works.name: UniDrive: Towards Universal Driving Perception Across Camera Configurations (arXiv 2410.13864)
closest_works.what_it_does: Plug-and-play input canonicalization: transforms original images into a unified set of virtual cameras via ground-aware projection (ground-plane assumption for below-horizon content), plus optimization of the virtual configuration to minimize expected projection error. Built and evaluated on a 160k-frame CARLA platform with varied camera configs; trained-on-one-config models generalize with minor degradation.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Direct overlap with C1: warping inputs to canonical virtual cameras using current extrinsics, train and test, on CARLA cross-config data. Also overlaps our benchmark contribution (CARLA cross-config evaluation with correct calibration = CTS-CAL).
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: UniDrive's warp uses a ground-plane homography (systematic distortion for above-ground structure); our C1 restricts to gravity-aligned pure-rotation homography, which is exact for rotation and degrades gracefully. UniDrive assumes correct extrinsics at test — no stale-extrinsic threat model, no self-calibration. It is a wrapper, not an analysis of why architectures differ. CoIn3D already reports beating it, so C1 alone cannot carry a paper; it is a component, with novelty in the rotation-only canonicalization choice and its interaction with C2-C4.

closest_works.name: CamShift dataset + Neural Rendering for Sensor Adaptation in 3D Object Detection (arXiv 2508.12695)
closest_works.what_it_does: CARLA benchmark with paired sim-SUB (subcompact) and sim-SUV splits of the SAME scenes — i.e., precisely our cross-platform CTS setting with correct calibration. Benchmarks detectors across paradigms; key empirical finding: dense-BEV backward-projection architectures (BEVFormer) are most robust to sensor-configuration change. Fix: NeRF-based pipeline that re-renders the entire training dataset to the target sensor setup.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Publishes (a) our CTS-CAL evaluation design (same-scene, two-platform CARLA) and (b) the empirical half of our mechanism finding — that backward/sampling-gated architectures degrade least. Our 'gates-sampling vs extract-then-place' split must be positioned as the code-verified causal explanation (incl. CAPE disproving the depth hypothesis and the BN(27) saturation analysis), not as the discovery of the ranking.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Their fix is dataset re-rendering to a KNOWN target config (forbidden by our constraint and requiring target knowledge); no architectural or test-time method, no stale-extrinsic axis, no mechanism beyond the ranking. Our 10-model breadth, VP-IMG/EXT/CAL factorization, and the zero-variance single-rig conditioning analysis go beyond it — but we must cite it prominently.

closest_works.name: RoboBEV: Towards Robust BEV Perception under Corruptions (arXiv 2304.06719; extended as 'Benchmarking and Improving BEV Perception Robustness', arXiv 2405.17426)
closest_works.what_it_does: The canonical BEV robustness benchmark: 8 image-level corruptions (bright, dark, fog, snow, motion blur, color quant, camera crash, frame lost) x 3 severities on nuScenes, across many detectors/segmenters. Findings: temporal fusion, pretraining, and depth-free view transforms improve robustness. No extrinsic/pose perturbation at all.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Owns the term 'BEV robustness' and the multi-model-benchmark paper format; its 'depth-free transforms are more robust' finding is an early echo of our mechanism claim. Reviewers will ask why our perturbations aren't in RoboBEV terms.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Pure corruption/noise threat model — pixels are corrupted but geometry stays consistent. It never breaks the image-extrinsic agreement (our VP-IMG) and never changes platform (CTS). We occupy the structured geometric-shift axis they explicitly lack. Adjacent: 'Understanding the Robustness of 3D Detection with BEV Representations' (CVPR 2023, arXiv 2303.17297) adds N(0,1.67°) roll/pitch extrinsic NOISE — still unstructured noise, analysis-only, no fix; and M-BEV/MetaBEV handle camera dropout, not pose.

closest_works.name: EAFormer: Epipolar Attention Field Transformers for BEV Semantic Segmentation (arXiv 2412.01595)
closest_works.venue_year: arXiv Dec 2024 (workshop/conference status unclear — verify before citing)
closest_works.what_it_does: Replaces learned positional encodings in attention-based BEV segmentation with analytic epipolar attention fields derived from camera geometry; +2% mIoU on map segmentation and explicitly demonstrates better transfer to entirely new camera setups (different extrinsics and intrinsics) than models that implicitly learn the camera configuration.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: This is C2 in published form: removing per-camera learned parameters (cams_embeds-style) because they bake in the training rig, replaced by analytic geometry. Same motivation, same conclusion.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Segmentation-only, single component, correct-calibration setting, no detection, no benchmark breadth, no stale-extrinsic handling. C2 must be framed as 'applying the (known) de-slotting principle systematically across paradigms and quantifying its share of the gap', not as a new idea.

closest_works.name: DG-BEV: Towards Domain Generalization for Multi-View 3D Object Detection in BEV (arXiv 2303.01686)
closest_works.what_it_does: Cross-dataset DG (nuScenes/Waymo/Lyft): decouples depth from focal length (scale-invariant depth), and — critically for us — 'dynamic perspective augmentation' that diversifies extrinsics via HOMOGRAPHY warps of training images, plus focal-length pseudo-domains with adversarial training. nuScenes→Waymo NDS* 0.415 vs 0.178 source-only.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: The homography-based extrinsic augmentation is exactly the 2D-warp augmentation our constraint permits and that C4's fine Delta-R regressor trains on. This is the mandatory 'extrinsic-aug baseline' our method must clearly exceed; its intrinsic-decoupled depth also anticipates parts of C3's analytic-scale argument.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Homography augmentation alone is exactly the baseline our diagnosis says is insufficient (it cannot synthesize translation/parallax and does not fix extract-then-place architectures' calib conditioning). DG-BEV is depth-paradigm-specific (CoIn3D shows it fails on BEVFormer/PETR), assumes correct test calibration, and has no test-time component. Successors PD-BEV (AAAI 2025, perspective debiasing via rendering BEV features to 2D heatmaps) and UDGA (arXiv 2410.22461, multi-view overlap depth) are the same correct-calibration, cross-dataset DG line.

closest_works.name: Mind the Hitch: Dynamic Calibration and Articulated Perception for Autonomous Trucks (dCAP, arXiv 2603.23711)
closest_works.what_it_does: For tractor-trailer rigs where trailer-camera pose changes continuously (fifth-wheel articulation), a transformer with cross-view + temporal attention regresses the 6-DoF tractor↔trailer relative pose at test time and feeds the dynamically predicted pose into BEVFormer through its standard calibration interface; introduces a CARLA benchmark (STT4AT) with time-varying inter-rig geometry.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Closest published precedent for C4's core move: estimating extrinsics at inference and injecting them into a BEV detector analytically. Also CARLA-based, also exploits cross-view consistency.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Trailer-specific (1-DoF-dominant articulation, dedicated pose network, known kinematic prior), not a general self-calibration of an arbitrary rig shift; no coarse analytic sweep over cached features scored in BEV space, no homography-trained Delta-R regression under a single-rig constraint, no cross-platform transfer. But it proves CVPR-level appetite for test-time-pose-into-BEV, so C4 must be carefully differentiated, and the classical online-calibration literature (ROECS, GSAlign, 'Towards Online Surround-View Calibration') must appear as baselines — reviewers WILL ask 'why not just run online calibration first?'

closest_works.name: Rig-Robust BEV Perception via 3D Gaussian Splatting and Cyclic Self-Supervision (Hafeez et al., Univ. of Galway)
closest_works.what_it_does: Sedan→SUV BEV segmentation transfer: lifts GaussianLSS features into a 3D Gaussian scene, renders rig-aware perspective features for both sedan and SUV, and cyclically fine-tunes with pseudo-SUV views through a frozen decoder (decoder dropped at inference). SUV IoU 23.46% with sedan-only data, 25.15% with 20% SUV RGB.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Same threat model as our CTS (sedan→SUV vehicle-platform transfer) under a near-identical single-rig training constraint, solved without external NVS data.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Feature-space rendering is still rendering-based augmentation in spirit (gray area for our constraint, but it is training-time and rig-targeted); segmentation-only, single model, low absolute numbers, minor venue. No detection, no stale extrinsics, no test-time calibration, no mechanism analysis. It confirms the niche is active but does not occupy our claims.

closest_works.name: CHARM3R: Towards Unseen Camera Height Robust Monocular 3D Detector (arXiv 2508.11185)
closest_works.what_it_does: Monocular 3D detection under out-of-distribution camera HEIGHT (CARLA, multiple heights): shows camera-relative regressed depth and ground-relative depth have opposite-signed error trends under height change and averages the two estimates, improving unseen-height generalization >45%.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Directly anticipates C3's central parameterization claim — that ground/height-anchored depth generalizes across rig pose where camera-relative depth fails — including using CARLA to isolate the geometric axis. The roadside line (BEVHeight CVPR 2023, BEVHeight++, CoBEV) made the same height-not-depth argument earlier for diverse mounting poses.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: All of these are monocular or roadside, none are multi-camera BEV with deformable-attention gating; C3's specific combination (DFA3D weight-path depth gating + height-above-ground parameterization with analytic metric scale + ray-direction-only conditioning) is unpublished as a package, but each ingredient must be attributed (DFA3D, BEVHeight, CHARM3R, Plücker-ray conditioning in CoIn3D). The zero-variance/BN-saturation argument for WHY rig-level conditioning fails under single-rig training appears to be ours alone.

closest_works.name: Calibration-free BEV line: CFT 'Multi-Camera Calibration Free BEV Representation' (arXiv 2210.17252), BEVSOC (IEEE 2024)
closest_works.what_it_does: Remove calibration inputs entirely and learn the view transform implicitly; CFT reports much smaller degradation than BEVFormer/PETR under extrinsic perturbation (e.g., other methods drop 0.6-7.6% NDS under noise while CFT is stable) at the cost of peak accuracy.
closest_works.overlap_with_ours: Represents the opposite pole of the design space we argue against (we keep analytic geometry and fix the conditioning instead); their perturbation experiments are an early stale-extrinsic-noise evaluation.
closest_works.what_remains_novel_for_us: Calibration-free models cannot exploit CORRECT new calibration (they have no CTS-CAL upside and cannot do C4 at all); our position — analytic geometry everywhere, learned components rig-agnostic, calibration recoverable at test time — is distinct and arguably the only one that benefits from both VP-IMG correction and CTS-CAL. Useful as a contrast baseline, not a threat.

litRobust.verdict: The threat model itself is no longer virgin territory: structured viewpoint shift was framed by NVIDIA at ICCV 2023, cross-platform transfer with correct calibration (our CTS-CAL) is now a published benchmark setting three times over (CamShift/IV 2025, UniDrive/ICLR 2025, CoIn3D/CVPR 2026), and even our architecture-ranking finding exists in empirical form (CamShift's 'backward projection is most robust', RoboBEV's 'depth-free transforms are more robust'). Likewise C1 (UniDrive's virtual cameras), C2 (EAFormer's analytic-instead-of-learned encodings), and C3's ingredients (DFA3D gating, BEVHeight/CHARM3R height parameterization, CoIn3D's Plücker-ray and ground-depth conditioning) each have a published near-equivalent, so C1-C3 individually are incremental and cannot carry a paper. What remains genuinely unoccupied, as far as this search shows, is the intersection we actually claim: (1) the VP-IMG setting — re-rendered viewpoint images with STALE extrinsics — is evaluated by nobody (RoboBEV-line noise keeps images consistent; all DG/config works assume correct calibration), and (2) test-time extrinsic SELF-calibration of a general multi-camera rig that converts VP-IMG toward CAL (C4: analytic Delta-R sweep on cached features + learned BEV scorer + homography-trained fine regression) has no general published instance — the nearest, dCAP (CVPR 2026), is trailer-articulation-specific with a dedicated pose network, and classical online surround-view calibration (ROECS/GSAlign) is an external module we must include as a baseline or the contribution is vulnerable. So the paper is viable only if C4 (+C5) and the causal mechanism analysis (gates-sampling vs extract-then-place, code-verified, with the single-rig zero-variance/BN-saturation explanation that no prior work states) are the centerpiece, with C1-C3 presented as a constraint-respecting recipe whose interaction effects are ablated. Two skeptical caveats: first, CoIn3D undermines the practical force of our 'no re-rendering' training constraint, because its training-free 3DGS augmentation also needs only single-rig data — we must either beat CDA-style augmentation head-to-head on our benchmark or justify the constraint on renderer-artifact/no-depth-pipeline/target-unknown grounds; second, the measured headroom (RRS 0.425→0.779) is our strongest selling point but it is an oracle bound — the paper stands or falls on how much of that gap the learned C4 actually closes against (a) homography extrinsic-aug baselines (DG-BEV) and (b) an off-the-shelf online-calibration-then-detect pipeline. Verdict: co-carry, yes — C4 + VP-IMG threat model + mechanism analysis together are a defensible CVPR/ICCV-level claim as of June 2026; C1-C3 alone, or the benchmark alone, would be scooped on arrival.

flaws.issue: Three verified facts make C1 net-negative as specified. (a) The sedan training rig is EXACTLY gravity-aligned (CAM_FRONT optical-axis elevation 0.000 deg, up_z=1.0000 in sedan_infos_val.pkl), so train-time canonicalization is exactly the identity: the backbone never sees warp resampling, stretched pixels, or invalid borders during training, but sees them at test — the claim '학습·추론 동일 적용' is internally false; it is a pure test-time distribution shift. (b) The benefit surface is a single cell: SUV is also gravity-aligned (elev 0 deg; only height 2.35m differs, which homography cannot touch) → C1 is a no-op for CTS-suv; under VP-IMG the believed (stale) extrinsics are gravity-aligned → canonicalization is again identity → no-op for the other target metric. (c) The one cell where C1 acts, CTS-bus (all 6 cams pitched −20 deg), requires a 20-deg pitch warp that invalidates 41.7% of pixels (measured: fx=953.4, 80x50.5 deg FOV) AND crops everything below virtual-FOV bottom −25.3 deg, i.e., all ground within 6.1–8.6 m of each camera (h=2.87–4.08 m) — the bus camera's entire near field. BEVFormer already achieves bus CAL 40.1 with NO canonicalization; C1 trades the pitch mismatch (which analytic sampling already handles) for 42% feature loss + OOD borders.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Cut C1 as a standalone component. If retained: (i) FOV-preserving virtual intrinsics (larger canvas / shifted principal point) instead of crop — but note this changes the ray field and breaks the 'identical rays' premise used elsewhere; (ii) mandatory train-time random rotation-homography augmentation so warp artifacts are in-distribution (allowed under the 2D-warp rule, and it is the same data C4(ii) needs anyway); (iii) demote to an optional final-pass re-warp inside C4 after Delta-R is estimated, and ablate against not warping at all.

flaws.issue: Shortcut learning makes the head untransferable as specified. Verified: VP variants are pure rotations about each camera's own optical center (translation delta = 0.0000 in viewpoint_metadata.json), so for in-FOV pixels homography synthesis is geometrically EXACT (zero parallax residual — the 1.6m/8-deg-pitch parallax worry is refuted by the data; under the counterfactual ego-pivot rotation, the 0.24m lever-arm translation would give 45 px parallax at 5m / 4.6 px at 50m, but that is not what the benchmark does). The real residual is the revealed band: a homography-warped training image has a deterministic invalid border whose geometry encodes Delta-R exactly (pitch 4→20 deg: 9.6%→41.7% of pixels; yaw: 7.7%→31.2%), plus a global resampling-blur signature. A re-rendered test image has REAL content in that band and native sharpness. A regression head trained on such pairs will read Delta-R off the border with ~zero train error and transfer ~nothing. The proposal text shows no awareness of this.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Train only on interior crops strictly inside the valid region (note this caps the trainable |Delta| — at 20 deg pitch only ~58% of rows survive, so large-angle supervision is structurally limited); alternatively inpaint/noise-fill borders AND apply identical warp-resample chains to Delta=0 samples so blur is uninformative. Mandatory acceptance test: evaluate the head on held-out RE-RENDERED VP data (never homography) before integrating; report this number in the paper.

flaws.issue: Near-horizon degeneracy on the training rig. Along a ray at elevation eps, dh/dd = −sin(eps); depth is recoverable from height only where |eps| is large. On the 1.6m sedan rig the 20–60m detection band sits almost on the horizon: ground-contact pixels of a car at 40m have eps=2.29 deg → a 0.1m height bin spans 2.5m of depth; car-body pixels at h≈1.2m have eps=0.57 deg → 10m of depth per 0.1m bin; pixels at h≈1.6m (roofs of cars, truck sides) have eps≈0 → depth strictly unobservable from height. DFA3D's 112 metric bins give a uniform ~0.5m. So the gate loses its entire purpose (disambiguating BEV cells along a ray, 5–50m apart with near-identical heights) exactly where most detections live. The genuinely good part — height labels are rig-invariant content (ground is h=0 from any camera) — does not rescue the discriminability problem.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Hybrid parameterization: height gate for steep rays (|eps| above a threshold; this is where the bus's high pitched-down cameras live, so CTS transfer keeps the benefit), inverse-depth/disparity gate near the horizon with analytic scale; or predict a joint (height, depth) distribution. Run the head-to-head ablation height vs metric vs hybrid on the same backbone — reviewers will demand it.

flaws.component: C3 weight-path gate x VP-IMG (pre-correction brittleness)
flaws.issue: The gate AMPLIFIES stale-extrinsic damage rather than buffering it. Gate value = predicted height probability evaluated at the analytic height of each sample point, computed from believed extrinsics. Under all-cam pitch 20 deg stale, sample heights are wrong by d*delta = 14m at 40m → the gate assigns ~0 weight to the correct features → the BEV is starved, whereas ungated BEVFormer degrades gracefully (its VR-pitch 0.191 is bad but nonzero; a hard multiplicative gate can be worse). Even post-C4, a 1 deg pitch residual gives 0.7m height error at 40m, several bins wide. The proposal predicts C3 improves IMG precision; pre-C4 it plausibly LOWERS VP-IMG below the gate-free baseline, and the DFA3D quadrant result that would test this is explicitly 'pending'.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Gate floor (1-alpha)+alpha*p or temperature so the gate can never zero out features; widen gate bins proportionally to d (uncertainty ∝ d*sigma_pitch); or apply hypothesis-consistent gating only after C4 has converged. Block the C3 claim on the DFA3D quadrant numbers.

flaws.issue: The single largest headroom chunk is the least observable. Measured BEVFormer all-cam per-axis: VR-yaw 0.527 → CR-yaw 0.938 (vs pitch 0.191→0.665, roll 0.557→0.733). But all-cam yaw rotates every camera about parallel gravity axes → relative inter-camera rotations are EXACTLY unchanged → cross-view overlap consistency is invariant; the only geometric residual comes from pivot offsets (camera baselines 0.4–1.7m): mismatch ≈ baseline*delta ≤ 0.6m at 20 deg, below one 2m cell of the 50x50 BEV. And a globally yawed scene is a geometrically self-consistent scene, so a BEV plausibility scorer has no geometric signal either. Recovery can only come from monocular content priors (road direction vs ego axis) — which will likely work on same-town CARLA val and is therefore the most benchmark-overfitted, least generalizable part of the method, yet it is sold as 'yaw 거의 전부 회수'. (Per-cam yaw IS observable via overlap mismatch — fine.)
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: State explicitly that all-cam yaw correction is a learned scene-prior estimator, not self-consistency; validate on held-out towns; if any temporal slack exists, ego-motion vs BEV-flow consistency observes common-mode yaw geometrically. Decompose the reported recovery per axis x protocol so the prior-driven part is visible.

flaws.component: C4(i) sweep combinatorics and the 'almost free' claim
flaws.issue: The benchmark's per-cam protocol (perturb ONE unknown camera, axis in {yaw,pitch,roll}, mag ±4..20) makes the hypothesis space 18-dimensional, not 3. A coordinate-descent sweep is 6 cams x 3 axes x 11 mags ≈ 198 BEV-encoder re-runs per iteration, x2 iterations ≈ 400 — plus per-hypothesis depth-head re-runs, since both the analytic sample heights and the per-pixel ray conditioning depend on the extrinsic hypothesis. At C2's demanded 1600x900 this is seconds-to-tens-of-seconds per frame; 'C-3: 자기보정은 거의 공짜다' is off by ~2 orders of magnitude for per-cam. Only the all-cam separable case (3x11=33 runs) is cheap. The GaussianLSS precedent is 11 candidates on ONE axis — a 36x smaller problem.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Run the regression head FIRST and use the sweep only as a local verification around its output (e.g., 3-5 candidates/axis); score per-camera BEV sectors so one encoder pass can score 6 per-camera hypotheses jointly; report a runtime table (ms/frame, passes) — a top-venue reviewer will demand it.

flaws.component: C4(i) x C1 x C3 cache coherence (internal contradiction)
flaws.issue: The sweep's economics rest on 'backbone features are extrinsic-independent, so cache once' (finding C-3). That is true of the 10 surveyed models but FALSE of the proposed model itself: C1 makes the backbone INPUT a function of the extrinsic hypothesis (canonicalization warp), and C3's depth head is conditioned on per-pixel rays computed from the hypothesis. So every sweep candidate evaluates a pipeline state (stale-canonicalized features + Delta-corrected sampling + stale ray conditioning) never seen in training, and the learned scorer is scoring out-of-training hybrids. The proposal never specifies which configuration the scorer is trained on.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Freeze canonicalization at the believed extrinsics during the sweep, train the scorer in exactly that (stale-canonical, Delta-at-projection) configuration, and re-run the full re-canonicalized pipeline ONCE at the argmax (+1 backbone pass). State this protocol explicitly; it also concretely costs C1 its 'analytic removal' elegance.

flaws.component: C4(i) learned BEV scorer failure modes + CAL no-harm
flaws.issue: (a) Sharper-but-wrong: a pitch-down hypothesis compresses ground features radially toward ego, increasing BEV activation density/sharpness — exactly the statistic a small CNN scorer latches onto; nothing constrains it to score geometric consistency. (b) CTS-CAL damage risk: under CTS-CAL the extrinsics are CORRECT, but bus/suv images are appearance-OOD for a scorer trained on sedan content only; if it selects Delta != 0 it degrades the one metric the proposal claims is 'guaranteed'. The text asserts 'CAL에선 Δ≈0을 예측해 무해' with no mechanism: Delta≈0 on clean input is NOT automatic — it requires explicit Delta=0 training samples and a do-nothing default.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Include Delta=0 (and pure-appearance-shift) samples in scorer/regressor training; margin-gated application (apply correction only if score beats the no-op hypothesis by a calibrated threshold); report CTS-CAL with C4 on AND off as a mandatory no-harm ablation.

flaws.issue: The anchor is ill-conditioned precisely where it is needed. Ground-intersection range sensitivity is ∂d/∂pitch = d²/h: at 40m with h=1.6m that is 17.5m per degree of residual pitch.
