After a 4-deg coarse sweep (±2 deg residual) the anchor is meaningless; sub-2m anchoring needs ≤0.1 deg pitch, and the 0.5m-AP regime needs ≈0.03 deg — far beyond the 2-deg-bin GaussianLSS precedent or any single-frame estimate. Under VP-IMG (before C4 converges) the believed ground plane is wrong by the full perturbation; under CTS-CAL the plane is correct but then C5 is largely redundant with correct analytic projection. Answering the posed question: the ground-plane estimate itself does NOT break under height change in CAL (z=0 ego plane comes from the given extrinsics; CARLA is flat), but it inherits the full stale-extrinsic error in IMG and a flat-plane assumption generally.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Demote C5 to a weak prior with range-dependent uncertainty (sigma_d ∝ d²·sigma_pitch/h) fused with the detector's own depth, or fold its cross-view gating half into C3's existing bev_mask hit-count normalization and cut the anchor head.

flaws.issue: Verified: cam_intrinsic is byte-identical across sedan/suv/bus and all VP variants (build_condition_pkls.py keeps it untouched 'because it is identical'), and C1 canonicalizes rotation. Therefore the per-pixel ray field is a fixed deterministic function of pixel coordinates — IDENTICAL at train and test. Answer to (5): the distribution is identical, so it is safe — but for the same reason it is information-free: it cannot adapt anything across rigs and reduces exactly to a positional encoding (CoordConv) plus a per-camera yaw constant (the cams_embeds replacement role, which is legitimate). The C-1 rule as stated ('condition only on inputs with within-rig variance') is necessary (prevents BN(27)-style saturation — that finding is solid) but NOT sufficient for useful conditioning; the proposal markets a constant input as 'normal-only에서도 일반화 가능한 조건부'. The actual fix in BEVDepth's failure is REMOVING the degenerate input, not adding rays.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Reposition: 'remove rig-level conditioning; replace camera-slot params with analytic ray/yaw encoding for camera identity'. Add the ablation ray-PE vs CoordConv vs none; if they tie (likely), say so — the honest version is still a contribution.

flaws.issue: Yes, warping requires consistent intrinsic/lidar2img updates: CarlaNuScenesDataset rebuilds lidar2img purely from sensor2lidar_rotation/translation + cam_intrinsic, so canonicalization must rewrite those pkl fields (K→K_virtual, R→gravity-aligned) or projections silently break. The warp must be composed with the rescale into ONE resampling (H_total = S·K_v·ΔR^T·K^{-1}); naive warp-then-resize double-interpolates, adding blur the (identity-warped) training pipeline never has — compounding the C4(ii) shortcut issue. Also C2 demands 1600x900 while the running BEVFormer-tiny config is 0.5-scale; the 4x backbone cost multiplies the C4 sweep cost.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Single composed warp; rewrite sensor2lidar+intrinsic fields atomically; pick and justify one resolution (the DETR3D high-res evidence is confounded — DETR3D differs in paradigm, not just resolution).

flaws.issue: Height-above-ground is unbounded for above-horizon rays (sky, infrastructure) and slightly wrong for objects on curbs/slopes; a height distribution needs a defined finite support with an overflow bin, and 'ground' must be defined (z=0 ego plane) — trivial in CARLA, a stated assumption for any generality claim.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: h ∈ [−1, +6]m with an overflow bin; state the flat-ground assumption explicitly in the paper.

flaws.issue: Two refinement iterations of a regressor applied to its own re-warped output have no convergence argument and each iteration adds a resampling pass (compounding blur) unless warps are composed; an overshooting head can oscillate between ±Delta.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Compose warps (never re-resample), damp the update (apply gamma·Delta, gamma≈0.7), and stop on score non-improvement from the C4(i) scorer.

flaws.issue: The VP benchmark is single-axis, rotation-only, about camera centers, on a fixed grid ±{4..20} deg — and the method's sweep grid, homography training, and axis-prioritized claims are tuned to exactly that family. Real miscalibration is combined-axis + translation, where homography synthesis is impossible and the sweep grid grows combinatorially. A reviewer will read the match between method assumptions and benchmark construction as overfitting to one's own benchmark.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Scope all claims to rotation miscalibration explicitly; add at least one combined-axis evaluation cell (the metadata grid permits composing variants only if rendered — otherwise test the Delta-R head on combined synthetic warps); discuss translation as out of scope with the parallax argument.

overclaims: '자기보정은 거의 공짜다' (C-3): true only for the all-cam separable sweep (~33 encoder re-runs); the benchmark's per-cam protocol needs ~200-400 re-runs per frame via coordinate descent, plus depth-head re-runs because ray conditioning and sample heights are hypothesis-dependent — and the proposed model breaks the very premise (extrinsic-independent backbone features) via C1.

'yaw 거의 전부 회수 (CAL-yaw ~0.95)': all-cam yaw — the largest headroom component (VR 0.527 → CR 0.938) — is exactly invisible to cross-view consistency (relative rotations unchanged; pivot-offset residual ≤0.6m, sub-BEV-cell) and to scene-plausibility scoring (a rotated scene is a valid scene); recovery rests entirely on same-town CARLA road-direction priors.

C1 '학습·추론 동일 적용': verifiably false — the sedan training rig is exactly gravity-aligned (elev 0.000 deg), so train-time canonicalization is the identity and test-time warps are out-of-distribution by construction.

C1 'CTS-CAL에선 pitch/roll 차이가 backbone 입력 단계에서 해석적으로 제거된다': only the bus has a rotation difference (suv is gravity-aligned → C1 no-op), and 'removal' of its 20-deg pitch costs 41.7% of pixels plus the entire near field (<6.1-8.6m) per camera.

'CTS-CAL은 C3만으로 현 최고선(suv ~77, bus ~40) 보장': 'guarantee' with an unvalidated height-parameterized gate whose depth discrimination collapses near the horizon, while the directly relevant evidence (DFA3D quadrant) is still pending; C4-on can additionally degrade CAL absent a no-harm gate.

'측정 헤드룸 0.425→0.779 회수': the 0.779 cap presumes near-oracle Delta-R on all axes including ±20 deg all-cam yaw; note even oracle extrinsics (CR) only reach pitch 0.665 / roll 0.733 because content has left the FOV — so the recoverable region is real but its composition (mostly the prior-driven yaw axis) is not stated.

'per-pixel ray 방향 조건화 = normal-only 학습에서도 일반화 가능한 조건부': with intrinsics identical across all platforms/variants (verified) and rotation canonicalized, the ray field is a constant function of pixel position — the conditioning is vacuous (a positional encoding), not a generalization mechanism.
'조사한 10개 모델 전부에서 backbone feature는 extrinsic-독립 → 캐시 탐색 저비용' applied to the proposed design: self-contradicted by C1 (extrinsic-dependent input warp) and C3 (ray-conditioned depth head).
missing: DFA3D quadrant results (the direct evidence for the weight-path-gate claim that C3 is built on) — currently 'pending' while C3's expected behavior is asserted; a reviewer will not accept the gate story without it, especially the pre-correction VP-IMG direction (gate could be worse than no gate).

Zero-training classical baselines for C4: (a) cross-camera feature matching in overlap regions → relative rotations (recovers per-cam errors and common pitch/roll directly; perturbations are pure rotations so this is well-posed), (b) horizon / vanishing-point pitch-roll estimation. The learned scorer+regressor must beat these or the learning is unjustified.
Held-out validation protocol for the Delta-R head on RE-RENDERED data (never homography) and on held-out towns — without it the border-shortcut and scene-prior overfitting concerns are unanswerable.
No-harm ablation on CTS-CAL with C4 enabled (margin-gated vs always-on vs off), plus explicit Delta=0 training-sample protocol.

Component-isolating ablations a reviewer will demand: ray-PE vs CoordConv vs none (C2); height vs metric-depth vs hybrid gate parameterization on the same backbone (C3); C1 on/off at fixed everything (its only active cell is CTS-bus); per-axis x per-protocol decomposition of C4 recovery so the prior-driven all-cam-yaw share is visible.

Per-cam protocol headroom: the BEVFormer full-val summary has mRRS = NaN (all-cam only was run); the method's claims should also be quantified on the per-cam cells where the search problem is 18-dimensional.
Runtime/compute table: 1600x900 x6 backbone + N-hypothesis sweep + 2 regression iterations, ms/frame and #passes per protocol; the 'almost free' narrative must be replaced by numbers.
Statistical rigor: cells are means over 10 signed magnitudes of a single run; seeds/error bars for the new model and for scorer argmax stability.

Scope statement vs real miscalibration: benchmark is single-axis, rotation-only, camera-center pivots, identical intrinsics; combined-axis, translation, and intrinsic drift are untested — claims must be scoped accordingly, and ideally one combined-axis probe added.
Any sim-to-real argument (or experiment) for the learned scorer and Delta-R priors — CARLA same-world training and evaluation inflates every learned-prior component.
revTech.keep_cut_recommendation: KEEP as core: (1) the analysis findings — the BN(27) 19-784-sigma saturation mechanism ('calibration-awareness != calibration-generalization'), the slot-prior inventory, and the gates-sampling vs extract-then-place split — this is the paper's strongest, code-verified material and survives review independently of the method. (2) C2 + C3-skeleton (remove slot-indexed params, analytic projection-sampling, DFA3D-style weight-path gate) as the architectural contribution, but with a HYBRID gate parameterization (height for steep rays / inverse-depth near horizon) instead of height-only, a gate floor for graceful degradation, and the claim gated on the DFA3D quadrant numbers. (3) C4 as the headline VP-IMG contribution, restructured: rig-level coarse sweep (cheap, 33 hypotheses) + shortcut-proofed Delta-R regression (interior-crop training, validated on re-rendered held-out data) + margin-gated application with Delta=0 training and a CTS-CAL no-harm ablation; report per-cam search honestly as coordinate descent with its real cost, and report all-cam yaw recovery separately as a scene-prior result. CUT: C1 as a standalone component — verified no-op for CTS-suv and for VP-IMG (stale extrinsics are gravity-aligned), identity at train time, and 41.7%-pixel + near-field loss in its only active cell (CTS-bus); at most fold a final FOV-preserving re-warp into C4's last iteration, with train-time warp augmentation. CUT/FOLD: C5 — the ground anchor is redundant under CAL (extrinsics given) and ill-conditioned under VP residual error (17.5 m range error per degree of pitch at 40 m); keep only its cross-view gating half, which is a one-line extension of BEVFormer's existing bev_mask hit-count normalization, inside C3. Net shape: benchmark + mechanism analysis + a two-component method (slot-free gated-sampling architecture, self-calibrating test-time rotation search) is a defensible top-venue package; the five-component version invites each weak part to drag down the strong ones.

flaws.issue: Five loosely-coupled components spanning input preprocessing, architecture surgery, depth parameterization, test-time optimization, and output refinement is a classic systems-paper profile. No single falsifiable claim carries the paper; reviewers will score each component against its own prior art (C1 ~ virtual-camera rectification / DG-BEV perspective debiasing, C3 height-param ~ BEVHeight + DFA3D gating + CamConvs-style ray conditioning, C2 is an ablation not a contribution) and find each individually incremental. Expected reviewer summary: 'well-engineered combination of known ideas, validated only on the authors' own simulator benchmark.'
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Pick one headline (recommended: C4 test-time rig self-calibration, see keep_cut). Demote C1-C3 to 'a calibration-faithful substrate' described in one subsection with a cumulative ablation table; cut C5 to a single ablation row or future work.

flaws.issue: The method is designed from, tuned on, and proposed to be validated on a benchmark built by the same authors, in simulation, with the target metrics (VP-IMG, CTS-CAL) defined by that benchmark. A CVPR/ICCV method paper cannot rest its entire empirical case on this loop: any positive result is consistent with 'the method overfits the diagnosis instrument.' This is the single most likely stated rejection reason.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: (a) Real-data leg: train on nuScenes, evaluate under injected extrinsic-noise protocols (RoboBEV-style) AND cross-dataset rig transfer nuScenes->Lyft/Waymo using the PD-BEV/DG-BEV protocol (the Generalizable-BEV fork is already in the repo). (b) Cross-model generality: plug C4 into 2-3 frozen public detectors (BEVFormer, DETR3D, DFA3D), not just the authors' model. (c) State a design-freeze: all hyperparameters fixed on CARLA before external evaluation. The CARLA benchmark then becomes the diagnostic, not the verdict.

flaws.issue: C4's cheapness rests on finding C-3: 'backbone features are extrinsic-independent in all 10 surveyed models, so cache features and sweep Delta-E through the BEV encoder only.' C1 destroys exactly this property: once the input is homography-warped using the current extrinsics, backbone features depend on the (stale, wrong) extrinsics. Sweeping Delta-R downstream of cached features then evaluates candidates against features extracted from a mis-canonicalized image. The two components as written contradict each other and a careful reviewer will catch it.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Either (a) apply candidate Delta-R as an additional image-space homography (rotation about camera center composes with the canonicalization warp), accepting at least one backbone re-extraction after the coarse step and counting it in the runtime budget; or (b) drop train-time canonicalization, keep C1 only as the test-time re-warp executed with the refined extrinsic estimate. Pick one and quantify the extra backbone passes.

flaws.issue: 'Pure rotation = exact homography' holds only for rotation about the camera center. The VP benchmark perturbs the rig: camera centers translate (lever arm), producing parallax and disocclusions that no homography generates. The Delta-R regression head is therefore trained on a systematically easier distribution than the test condition; the residual grows with perturbation magnitude and scene proximity. Same caveat applies to C1's claim that canonicalization 'analytically removes' target-rig pitch/roll in CTS-CAL — it removes the rotation component only, and costs FOV/resolution at image borders.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: State the approximation explicitly. Quantify the homography-vs-rerender gap (evaluate the Delta-R head on a held-out re-rendered subset vs warped-image subset, report per-axis error). Report FOV loss from canonicalization. If the gap is large, the coarse BEV-space sweep (which sees real re-rendered features) must carry the load and the paper should say so.

flaws.issue: The rule ('never condition learned modules on rig-level vectors') is induced from n=2 models — BEVDet and BEVDepth, which share the same BN1d(27)+MLP+SE code lineage, so effectively n=1 mechanism family. The 19-784 sigma saturation is confounded with a BatchNorm-on-zero-variance-input pathology: a reviewer will ask whether replacing BN with fixed normalization (or just removing BN) rescues rig-vector conditioning, which would reduce the 'design rule' to a normalization bug report. CAPE's QcR is a different instance but its failure is entangled with slot embeddings and intrinsic-only key PE, so it is not a clean third data point.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Run the controlled 2x2: same architecture with {no conditioning, rig-vector conditioning w/ BN, rig-vector conditioning w/ proper fixed normalization, per-pixel ray conditioning}, trained single-rig, evaluated on CTS-CAL. Only if ray-conditioning beats fixed-norm rig-conditioning does the rule survive as a principle; otherwise present it as a failure-mode analysis, not a law.

flaws.issue: The training constraint explicitly allows 2D warps. The strongest cheap competitor is therefore: jitter extrinsics during training WITH the matching homography image warp (consistent augmentation). The proposal's anti-pattern E.5 only rules out image-invariant extrinsic jitter (the CAPE-degeneracy case); the consistent variant is legal under the stated constraints, trivial to implement, and may capture a large share of C1+C4's benefit without any test-time machinery. If the paper does not include it and beat it, reviewers will assume it wins.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Add warp-consistent extrinsic augmentation as a first-class baseline (and as an ablation inside the proposed model). Also add: PD-BEV/DG-BEV, BEVHeight, UniDrive-style virtual cameras, GaussianLSS scorer extended to 3 axes, an off-the-shelf online extrinsic calibration method feeding a frozen detector, and a generic TTA baseline (e.g., Tent).

flaws.component: C4 no-harm claim on correct calibration
flaws.issue: 'On CAL the module predicts Delta~0 and is harmless' is asserted, not measured. A learned BEV scorer can prefer a nonzero Delta on correctly-calibrated inputs (scene-dependent score landscapes, degenerate texture, night), which would damage CTS-CAL — one of the two headline metrics — and clean in-distribution performance. This converts the method's safety into an empirical question the proposal treats as settled.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Measure the false-correction rate and the clean-data NDS delta with C4 enabled. Add a confidence threshold / hysteresis (only apply Delta if score margin exceeds tau) and report the tradeoff curve. Report multi-seed error bars — the team's own benchmark shows 0.0007-NDS margins flipping rank correlations, so single-run deltas are not evidence.

flaws.issue: The weight-path depth gating choice is justified by a quadrant prediction whose controlling experiment (DFA3D full VP/CTS) is marked '평가 예정' (pending) in both the proposal's Table B and SECTION5_ANALYSIS_KR.md:124. Building a design pillar on an unrun control, then citing it, is exactly the kind of forward reference reviewers attack.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Complete the DFA3D evaluation before writing the method section (training reportedly finished 06-11 per the analysis doc). If the quadrant prediction fails (weight-path gating does not preserve CAL recovery), C3's depth design needs rework, which is cheaper to discover now.

flaws.issue: Underspecified relative to the others: no loss, no architecture, no expected numbers, motivated only by 'IMG errors are positional (mATE x1.6).' Reads as padding and dilutes the contribution statement; also overlaps C4 (both correct geometric placement).
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Cut from the contribution list. If translation recovery matters empirically, fold a minimal version into C4 as a final translation step and report it as one ablation row.

flaws.issue: Bundling 1600x900 resolution into the method confounds every comparison: gains attributable to compute will be (correctly) discounted. DETR3D's bus advantage in Table B is the proposal's own evidence that resolution alone moves the target metric.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Resolution-matched comparisons throughout: every baseline at the same input resolution as the proposed model, plus one row showing the method at the baseline's native resolution.

flaws.issue: 'Self-calibration is nearly free' is unquantified. A 3-axis coarse grid is combinatorial (e.g., 11^3 = 1331 BEV-encoder passes if done jointly), plus 2 fine iterations, plus backbone re-extraction if the C1 inconsistency is fixed via re-warping. The GaussianLSS precedent swept 11 candidates on ONE axis.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Specify axis-separable or coordinate-descent sweep, report a latency/memory table (base forward vs +C4 coarse vs +C4 full), and a deployment story (per-frame vs drift-triggered calibration).

flaws.issue: The PitchBinClassifier/BEVScorer is cited from 'the GaussianLSS CARLA variant' (calibration.py:157-211). If that module lives in the team's own CARLA port rather than the upstream authors' release, calling it an external precedent is self-citation dressed as prior art and will be flagged if discovered.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Verify provenance against upstream GaussianLSS. If it is the team's own addition, present it honestly as the team's prototype, which is fine — it just isn't independent evidence.

flaws.issue: A known carla_VR 2x frame-misalignment bug previously invalidated committed VP VR/CR (image-swap) numbers (inflated collapse). The proposal's design decisions are driven by IMG/CAL figures (0.425/0.779, per-axis tables); any figure predating the frame-fix is suspect.
flaws.fix_or_mitigation: Audit every number cited in the proposal and paper against post-fix runs (the git history shows 'corrected BEVDet (frame-fix)' — extend the audit to all models/conditions) and state the audit in the supplement.

overclaims: The 0.425 -> 0.779 'headroom' is an oracle bound obtained by handing the model ground-truth extrinsics (VP-CAL), including the translation component and exact rotation. C4 estimates rotation only, approximately, from a learned scorer/regressor; realized recovery will be some unknown fraction, concentrated in yaw (their own axis analysis: CAL-yaw ~0.95 vs pitch/roll much harder). Stating 0.779 as the method's target invites reviewers to compute the realized fraction and call the paper overclaimed. Additionally, the ceiling was measured on vanilla BEVFormer — the modified model (C1-C3) has a different IMG floor and CAL ceiling.

'CTS-CAL is guaranteed at the current best line (suv ~77 / bus ~40) by C3 alone' — a performance guarantee for an unbuilt model, extrapolated from cross-model correlation, not from any run of the proposed architecture.

The conditioning-variance rule presented as a general design law ('rig-level vectors forbidden as learned-module inputs') is induced from two sibling codebases sharing one BN(27)+MLP implementation, with the BatchNorm pathology unconfounded from conditioning per se. As written it is an engineering heuristic with n~1 mechanistic evidence.

'Self-calibration is almost free' (C-3) — true only while backbone features are extrinsic-independent, a property the proposal's own C1 removes; joint 3-axis sweep cost and fine-iteration cost are never quantified.

'Pure rotation = exact homography' elides that VP perturbs the rig (camera centers translate -> parallax/disocclusion), so the Delta-R head trains on an easier distribution than it is tested on; canonicalization likewise removes only the rotational part of cross-platform geometry change.
'On CAL the module predicts Delta~0 and is harmless' — an untested no-harm claim protecting one of the two headline metrics.
C3's weight-path gating benefit is asserted while its controlling experiment (DFA3D full VP/CTS) is still pending in the proposal's own tables.

Implicit external validity: every quantitative claim comes from the authors' own CARLA re-rendering benchmark; nothing yet shows the failure modes or the fixes transfer to real imagery or real rig changes.

'Backbone features are extrinsic-independent in all 10 models' is used as a load-bearing premise for cheap test-time search, but the paper's own first component (C1) invalidates it for the proposed model.
missing: Real-data validation: nuScenes training with (a) injected extrinsic-noise robustness protocol and (b) cross-dataset rig transfer nuScenes->Lyft/Waymo under the PD-BEV/DG-BEV protocol; without at least one real-data leg the paper is a simulation study.

The warp-consistent extrinsic-augmentation baseline (extrinsic jitter WITH matching homography image warp — legal under the stated '2D warps allowed' constraint and plausibly captures much of C1+C4's benefit).

Method baselines: PD-BEV/DG-BEV (already cloned in repo as Generalizable-BEV), BEVHeight (C3 borrows its height parameterization), UniDrive-style unified virtual cameras, GaussianLSS scorer extended to 3 axes, an off-the-shelf online extrinsic-calibration method feeding a frozen detector, and a generic TTA baseline (Tent-style) — plus oracle-Delta and random-Delta bounds bracketing C4.

Per-axis recovery decomposition for C4: realized RRS vs oracle CAL for yaw/pitch/roll/translation separately, with the honest statement of what is unrecoverable (translation, content/parallax component).

Runtime and memory analysis: sweep size x BEV-encoder cost, fine-iteration cost, backbone re-extraction cost after the C1 fix, end-to-end latency vs base model, and a deployment policy (per-frame vs drift-triggered).
The controlled C-1 experiment isolating BatchNorm pathology from conditioning choice (no-cond / rig-cond+BN / rig-cond+fixed-norm / ray-cond), without which the headline design rule is anecdote.

Clean in-distribution non-regression: NDS on normal data for the full system (especially C2 slot-param removal and C4-enabled inference) vs BEVFormer/DFA3D baselines, with multi-seed error bars (their own benchmark shows rank correlations hinging on a 0.0007 NDS margin).

Failure-case analysis: scenes where the BEV scorer selects wrong Delta (night, textureless, degenerate score landscapes), behavior under combined rotation+translation perturbation, bus-height parallax limit.

Identifiability/justification at the level top venues expect for a geometry paper: which Delta components are observable from BEV-space consistency (yaw vs pitch/roll vs translation), the pitch-vs-height ambiguity at range, and why BEV-space scoring is necessary (the CAPE key-side-blindness argument, formalized).
Completed DFA3D quadrant result (currently '평가 예정') before C3's gating choice is citable.
Resolution-matched comparisons so gains are not attributable to the 1600x900 compute bump.
A design-freeze/preregistration statement and provenance audit (post frame-fix numbers only) to defuse the same-authors-benchmark circularity.
revAC.keep_cut_recommendation: KEEP AS HEADLINE — C4 (test-time extrinsic self-calibration in BEV space), reframed as Framing A: 'Test-time rig self-calibration for multi-camera BEV perception.' It is the only component that (i) attacks VP-IMG, the metric where every surveyed model collapses to ~0.32-0.43, (ii) has a crisp mechanism story grounded in the CAPE finding that extrinsic error is unobservable image-side and must be scored in BEV space, and (iii) can be demonstrated as a plug-in on multiple frozen public detectors (BEVFormer/DETR3D/DFA3D) and on nuScenes with injected noise — which simultaneously fixes the circularity problem. Headline claim: 'stale-extrinsic viewpoint shift is largely a recoverable calibration error: a cheap BEV-space search plus homography-trained refinement recovers X% of the oracle-calibration gap at Y ms overhead, across N detectors.' Required experiments: plug-in on 2-3 frozen detectors, nuScenes extrinsic-noise + cross-dataset transfer, per-axis recovery vs oracle, latency table, no-harm-on-correct-calib measurement, vs online-calibration and warp-consistent-augmentation baselines. Biggest rejection risk: realized recovery is mostly yaw and a small fraction of the 0.354 oracle gap, making gains look thin — mitigate by reporting honest per-axis decomposition and by the cross-detector generality. KEEP AS SUBSTRATE (one subsection + cumulative ablation, not contributions) — C2 slot-param removal and C3's analytic-projection + weight-path depth gating: they define the 'calibration-faithful base model' that makes C4's analytic sweep meaningful, but each is individually prior art (BEVFormer sampling, DFA3D gating, BEVHeight height-param, CamConvs ray conditioning); claiming them as contributions invites a novelty kill. FOLD — C1 into C4: the homography machinery is identical (canonicalization = applying the warp at the current extrinsic estimate; candidate Delta-R = composing another homography), and folding resolves the C1/C4 cached-feature contradiction by making the warp part of the calibration loop rather than a separate training-time component. CUT — C5 entirely (underspecified, overlaps C4's purpose; keep at most one ablation row for a translation step). DEMOTE — the C-1 conditioning-variance finding from 'design rule' to a Discussion/analysis subsection with the BN-confound control experiment; if that controlled experiment comes out clean, it is the best single paragraph in the paper ('calibration-awareness does not imply calibration-generalization'), but it cannot be a contribution claim at n=2 sibling implementations. Two fallback framings if C4's realized recovery is small: Framing B 'calibration-generalizable BEV by construction' (C1+C2+C3 core, CTS-CAL + real cross-rig transfer vs PD-BEV/BEVHeight; risk: bag-of-known-tricks novelty kill and it abandons VP-IMG entirely) and Framing C 'diagnostic paper: why calibration-aware BEV fails to generalize, with surgical interventions as causal proof' (scientifically strongest, but it is a benchmark/analysis paper, not the method paper requested, and circularity is worst there without real data). Decision gate: run C4 standalone on frozen BEVFormer first (smallest diff, the BEVScorer precedent code already exists); if it recovers >=50% of the IMG->CAL gap on yaw+pitch, commit to Framing A; if not, pivot to Framing B with the real cross-rig transfer leg as the centerpiece.
